item.text: Reliable postal services made long-distance relationships more regular, personal, and durable. Before dependable mail routes, news traveled slowly and unpredictably, so separation often weakened family ties, friendships, business partnerships, and courtships. Cheaper, scheduled delivery allowed people to exchange letters frequently, share everyday experiences, offer emotional support, and coordinate practical decisions across great distances. Migrants could remain involved with relatives at home, while soldiers and travelers could sustain connections during long absences. Letters also created records of affection, obligations, and shared events that could be reread and preserved. Postal networks supported broader communities too: people joined clubs, exchanged ideas, and maintained professional contacts without meeting in person. Distance did not disappear, but reliable correspondence made it far less socially isolating.
